clue.text: Some golfers play thus night and day

definitions.meaning: a golf practice game in which putts are taken from points circling the hole like the hours on a dial
continuously, all twenty-four hours without a break

explanation.definitionFit: A putting drill moves round the hole like a dial's hours, and the same phrase means working nonstop through every hour.

clue.text: Child's garment brought in from Persia

indicators.note: brought in means the letters are found carried inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A child's outfit imported from Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece playsuit worn by toddlers.

clue.text: Hare found in unusual form not previously encountered

indicators.note: in unusual form means the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A hare is found looking strange, something never seen before.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprecedented, never known before.

clue.text: Tube used to carry a coin, once

indicators.note: used to carry means the tube holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a duct is a tube

explanation.surface: A pipe was formerly used to transport a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold piece formerly used in European trade.

clue.text: Surrender Hampshire's leader to Hampshire town

indicators.note: Hampshire's leader means the first letter of that word

parts.note: Andover is a market town in Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Give up the county's chief to one of its towns.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give up or relinquish control.

clue.text: Designing vessel takes a year

parts.note: a craft is a boat or vessel
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Designing a boat takes twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: Designing in the sense of scheming, cunning.

clue.text: Box in Scotland's unmatched players

indicators.note: in means the box goes inside the Scots word

parts.note: orra is a Scots word for odd, unmatched
a chest is a box

explanation.surface: A box sits among Scotland's unrivalled musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of instrumentalists playing together.

clue.text: Liquid from well raised with iron tool

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ink comes from an inkwell
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Water drawn from a well and brought up with an iron implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A bladed cutting implement.

clue.text: Fashion models, infrequently

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means shape anew, so the letters are remade

explanation.surface: Fashion models are rarely seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely, not often.

clue.text: Complain about this Latin hair style

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other, so the complaint wraps the Latin word

parts.note: to complain is to moan
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a classical scholar's haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of upright hair down the middle of a shaved head is named after a Native American people.

clue.text: Records vault I have produced

parts.note: a vault is an arched roof, an arch
contracted to I've

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of the vault they built to store records.
explanation.definitionFit: Stored historical documents kept by an institution form its files of records.

clue.text: Demand cutback by Eastern state

parts.note: the single word splits in two: axe (a chop) followed by back, which turns that word round
CT is Connecticut, a state on the US east coast

explanation.surface: Someone demands a spending reduction from an eastern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutback' looks like one word for a reduction, but split it: AXE (cut) read back gives EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact payment is to require or insist upon it forcibly.

clue.text: With other people coming in, continually improving

indicators.note: coming in means the people are placed inside the phrase meaning continually

parts.note: on end means continually, as in for hours on end
them, as opposed to us, means other people

explanation.surface: With newcomers arriving, things keep getting better.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone recovering from illness is getting better, steadily mending.

clue.text: Measure introduced by party is an evasive move

indicators.note: introduced by means the party word comes first, ahead of the measure

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute
a step is a measure taken

explanation.surface: A party brings in a policy measure that dodges the issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging a blow or a question by moving aside is an evasion.

clue.text: Youth — a boy daughter speaks about

indicators.note: about means the speaking word wraps round the rest

parts.note: says means speaks
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Youth, says a daughter about a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: One's carefree, inexperienced younger years.

clue.text: A lot of pupils taking course

definitions.meaning: a group of schoolchildren sorted by ability into one teaching set

explanation.definitionFit: Schools sort pupils by ability into bands, and a brook or flowing watercourse carries the same name.

clue.text: Taken up, green sods get relaid

indicators.note: get relaid means the letters are laid down again in another order

explanation.surface: Lifted turf is relaid in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbed, fully occupied in attention.

clue.text: Happy to attend clubs, as long as I get admitted

indicators.note: get admitted means the condition and I are let inside the other pieces

parts.note: be at means to attend
C is the card abbreviation for clubs
if means as long as, provided

explanation.surface: Glad to go to the clubs, provided I get in.
explanation.definitionFit: Blissful, radiantly joyful, like a saint.

clue.text: Creature who's mischievous and incredible sent round puzzle

indicators.note: sent round means the whole string of pieces is turned back to front

parts.note: an elf is a mischievous sprite
fab, short for fabulous, means incredible

explanation.surface: An impish, unbelievable creature is sent round a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creature who's mischievous' looks like part of the definition, but it is a piece; 'sent round' turns the whole joined string, not just the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To puzzle someone is to bewilder or perplex them.

clue.text: Quarrel with composer about note

indicators.note: about means the composer goes round the note

parts.note: Bach, the German Baroque composer
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Arguing with a composer over a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift, a falling-out between parties.

clue.text: Disorganised rag ended in chaos

indicators.note: in chaos means the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A disorganised student magazine finished in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'rag' is a student newspaper or charity event in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown into disorder or madness is disarranged, disorganised.

clue.text: Nureyev, for one, read Sun irregularly

indicators.note: irregularly means the letters are arranged in a different order

explanation.surface: A famous dancer reads a tabloid now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, which disguises the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was a celebrated male ballet dancer.

clue.text: Foreign cash put into plant

indicators.note: into means the put word goes inside the plant

parts.note: a pea is a plant
set means put

explanation.surface: Foreign money is put into a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The former currency unit of Spain.

clue.text: Shift mark from former triangular part of building

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: from means the mark is taken out of the building part

parts.note: a pediment is the triangular gable over a classical portico
M stands for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone moves a mark from an old gable of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' reads as a verb but is the noun: a contrivance or makeshift.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift in the old sense is a stratagem or makeshift device, a convenient means.

clue.text: Climbing mountain, I had warm cover over shoulder

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
contracted to I'd

explanation.surface: Climbing a mountain, I wore a warm wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartan woollen shawl worn over the shoulder in the Highlands.

clue.text: With triumph, instal leader of nation

definitions.meaning: a ... glory or title won, a victory
to put a monarch on the throne formally

explanation.definitionFit: A champion wins the title as a prize, and a coronation puts a sovereign formally on the throne.

clue.text: Engineers splitting specialised railway carriage and tender

indicators.note: splitting means the engineers break into the carriage word

parts.note: a car is a railway carriage for a special use, such as a dining car
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Engineers working on a carriage and locomotive tender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' suggests a locomotive coal truck, but means one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is someone who looks after another person.

clue.text: Riddle of domestic assistant I dismissed

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman, a domestic help

indicators.note: dismissed means the I is sent away from the assistant

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: Puzzle of the cleaner sacking her assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'char' (charwoman) is British for a cleaner; 'I' is named and removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A game of mimed syllables to be guessed is a riddle acted out.

clue.text: Anticipate having products of mine included in payment

indicators.note: included in means the mine products are placed inside the payment

parts.note: a fee is a payment
ores are dug from a mine

explanation.surface: Someone expects mine output to be part of their payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate is to see coming, predict.

clue.text: Courier needing efficiency, and something added

parts.note: dispatch means speed and efficiency
a rider is a clause added to a document

explanation.surface: A courier needs efficiency, plus a bit extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcyclist carrying urgent packages is a messenger.
